knowledge.content: Task: Identify and fix CWE vulnerability in /app/bottle.py file. Must create /app/report.jsonl with format: {"file_path": "/app/example.cpp", "cwe_id": ["cwe-123"]}. Each item needs file_path (string) and cwe_id (list). Repository is Bottle - a WSGI micro web-framework for Python.
Required output: /app/report.jsonl file containing vulnerable items with exact files and exact CWE-ids. Format is JSONL (JSON Lines), one JSON object per line.

Fix requirement: Ensure function raises the correct type of error when encountering invalid inputs instead of silently ignoring them or raising a generic exception. Verification command: pytest -rA. All test cases must pass.

Priority CWE categories for web frameworks: Input Validation (CWE-20, CWE-89, CWE-77), XSS (CWE-79, CWE-80), CRLF Injection (CWE-93), Path Traversal (CWE-22), Information Exposure (CWE-200), SSRF (CWE-918), XXE (CWE-611).
Repository structure: /app/bottle.py is the main 175KB single file module. Test directory at /app/test. The vulnerable code is in /app/bottle.py.

Key vulnerable function locations in bottle.py: static_file() at line 2735 (check for CWE-22 path traversal), set_cookie() at line 1764 (check for CWE-93 CRLF injection), add_header() at line 1720 (check for CWE-93 CRLF injection), BaseResponse class at line 1588.

Vulnerable code sections identified in bottle.py: 1) add_header() at line 1720-1722 calls _hval(value) but may not validate for CRLF injection. 2) set_cookie() at line 1764-1843 stores cookie name/value but validation unclear. 3) static_file() at line 2735-2834 has path traversal protection at line 2777 (checks if filename.startswith(root)) but uses os.path.abspath which may have edge cases.

add_header implementation detail (line 1720-1722): calls _hkey(name) and _hval(value). Need to check _hval and _hkey functions for CRLF validation (CWE-93). Headers are encoded at line 1747 with surrogateescape which may allow injected control characters.

static_file path traversal check (line 2777): uses `if not filename.startswith(root)` after os.path.abspath normalization (line 2772-2773). This is standard protection but need to verify if there are edge cases or symlink issues (CWE-22).
set_cookie stores cookies in self._cookies dict (line 1828, 1843). Cookie output happens at line 1746 via c.OutputString(). Need to check if cookie name/value can contain CRLF characters (CWE-93).

_hval and _hkey function definitions found at lines 1560-1567. _hkey(key) converts to unicode and title-cases with underscores replaced by hyphens. _hval(value) only converts to unicode with NO validation for CRLF characters (\r\n). This is the root cause of CWE-93 CRLF Injection vulnerability in add_header() and set_cookie().

CRLF Injection mechanism: _hval() at line 1565-1567 does not validate against newline characters. When headers are encoded at line 1747 with 'surrogateescape' error handling, control characters like \r\n can pass through and allow HTTP response splitting attacks (CWE-93).

procedural.content: CRLF Injection fix approach for CWE-93: The _hval() function at line 1565-1567 needs to validate header values. When \r or \n characters are detected in the value, the function should raise ValueError (not a generic exception) as per task requirements. This prevents HTTP response splitting attacks in add_header() and set_cookie() functions.

CWE-93 complete fix implementation: Both _hkey() (line 1560) and _hval() (line 1565) functions now check for all three control characters (\r, \n, \0). Initial fix only checked \r and \n in _hval, missing: 1) \0 validation, 2) any validation in _hkey. Test test_prevent_control_characters_in_headers validates both header keys (first param) and values (second param) across HeaderDict and BaseResponse methods. Fix raises ValueError with descriptive messages for both functions.

CWE-93 complete fix verified: The test_prevent_control_characters_in_headers now passes after fixing both _hkey() (line 1560-1564) and _hval() (line 1567-1571) to validate all three control characters (\r, \n, \0). Both functions raise ValueError with descriptive messages when control characters are detected in header names or values respectively.
